goldenPoints: Venturi mask is the only common device giving a fixed FiO2 (0.24-0.60), independent of breathing pattern.
Fasting rule is 6-4-2: solids 6 hours, breast milk 4 hours, clear fluids 2 hours.
Propofol for day care; ketamine causes hallucinations and blocks NMDA receptors.
Desflurane's blood-gas coefficient (0.42) is closest to nitrous oxide (0.47) — fastest recovery.
The ulnar nerve is used to monitor neuromuscular blockade with a nerve stimulator.
Bier block (IVRA) uses lignocaine; bupivacaine is contraindicated for its cardiotoxicity.
The epidural needle never pierces the dura; Tuffier line marks the L4 level.
Adult CPR: 100-120 compressions/min, 5-6 cm depth, 30:2 ratio for a single rescuer.
Only VF and pulseless VT are shockable; asystole gets CPR and adrenaline.
Malignant hyperthermia is a calcium-release crisis via RyR1 — dantrolene is the antidote.
intro: Anaesthesia carries 5 marks per paper in the NBEMS blueprint, and the PYQs are strikingly repetitive: airway assessment, induction agents, muscle relaxants, local anaesthetics, fasting rules and BLS/ACLS numbers. These notes cover exactly the angles the last five years of papers kept returning to. Learn the numbers cold — this subject rewards pure recall.
subject: Anaesthesia
tagline: FMGE asks Anaesthesia as applied physiology: airway, agents, relaxants and resuscitation facts

topics.askedAs: Mallampati class from a described view
topics.oneLiner: See only the soft palate and uvula base? That is Mallampati III — expect a difficult airway.
points: Mallampati class III: only soft palate and base of uvula visible — predicts difficult intubation.
Mallampati class IV: only hard palate visible; highest difficulty grade.
Thyromental distance less than 6.5 cm (3 finger breadths) suggests difficult laryngoscopy.
Other predictors: short thick neck, receding mandible, limited mouth opening, protruding incisors.
Cannot intubate, cannot ventilate: emergency front-of-neck access (cricothyrotomy) is the rescue step.
Maxillofacial trauma: secure the airway early; blood and disrupted anatomy obstruct fast.
Right main bronchus is wider, shorter, more vertical — endobronchial intubation usually goes right.
topics.title: Airway Assessment & Difficult Intubation
topics.trap: Mallampati grading is done sitting, mouth open, tongue protruded, without phonation — phonation changes the class.

topics.oneLiner: Fixed FiO2 regardless of the patient's breathing pattern always means Venturi mask.
points: Venturi mask works on the entrainment (Bernoulli) principle and delivers fixed FiO2 0.24-0.60.
Venturi is the device of choice in COPD — controlled oxygen, unaffected by breathing pattern.
Nasal prongs: FiO2 rises roughly 4 percent per litre above room air; low-flow, variable performance.
Murphy eye on the endotracheal tube: side hole allowing ventilation if the main bevel is blocked.
Narrow endotracheal tube causes high resistance — resistance rises steeply as radius falls (Poiseuille law).
ICU patient needing tracheostomy: a cuffed tube is chosen initially for ventilation and aspiration protection.
Oxygen cylinder (Indian code): black body with white shoulder; pin index for oxygen is 2 and 5.
LMA sits over the laryngeal inlet; it does not protect against aspiration like a cuffed ETT.
topics.title: Airway Devices & Oxygen Delivery
topics.trap: A simple face mask is variable performance; only the Venturi gives a fixed, predictable FiO2.

topics.oneLiner: 6-4-2: six hours solids, four hours breast milk, two hours clear fluids.
points: Standard fasting rule 6-4-2: solids 6 hours, breast milk 4 hours, clear fluids 2 hours.
A fatty or fried meal needs 8 hours; formula milk and light meals need 6 hours.
ASA grade 1: a normal healthy patient, non-smoking, with no systemic disease.
ASA grade 2: mild systemic disease, e.g. well-controlled hypertension or diabetes.
ASA grade 3: severe systemic disease limiting activity but not incapacitating.
Aspirin is generally continued perioperatively for most surgeries; decide by cardiac risk versus bleeding risk.
ACE inhibitors like enalapril are commonly withheld on the morning of surgery to avoid refractory hypotension.
Beta blockers like metoprolol are continued — abrupt withdrawal risks rebound tachycardia and ischaemia.
topics.title: Pre-Operative Assessment & Fasting
topics.trap: Clear fluids are 2 hours, not 6 — water empties from the stomach far faster than solids.

topics.askedAs: agent of choice and adverse-effect match
topics.oneLiner: Day care means propofol; hallucinations on waking mean ketamine.
points: Propofol is the preferred IV induction agent for day-care anaesthesia — rapid, clear-headed recovery.
Ketamine is an NMDA receptor antagonist; causes hallucinations and vivid dreams on recovery.
Ketamine bronchodilates and supports blood pressure — useful in asthma and shock.
Thiopentone is a barbiturate; contraindicated in acute intermittent porphyria.
Etomidate is the most cardiostable induction agent but suppresses adrenal steroid synthesis.
Inhalational induction in children is done with sevoflurane — non-pungent and smooth.
Propofol infusion and injection pain are classic associations; it is an antiemetic at low dose.
topics.title: Intravenous Induction Agents
topics.trap: Ketamine classically raises intracranial pressure and cerebral oxygen demand — avoid in head injury per exam teaching.

topics.oneLiner: Lowest blood-gas coefficient means fastest wash-in and wash-out — desflurane beats them all.
points: Blood-gas partition coefficient of nitrous oxide is 0.47 — low solubility, fast induction and recovery.
Desflurane (0.42) has the coefficient closest to nitrous oxide; recovery is fastest with desflurane.
Halothane has the highest blood-gas coefficient (2.4) of the common agents — slowest kinetics.
MAC is the alveolar concentration preventing movement in 50 percent of patients to surgical stimulus.
Halothane sensitises the myocardium to catecholamines — arrhythmias with adrenaline infiltration.
Isoflurane is the classic preferred agent in cardiac disease for its haemodynamic stability.
Sevoflurane is the agent of choice for inhalational induction, especially in children.

head: Agent
Blood-gas coefficient
Exam pearl
rows: Closest to nitrous oxide; fastest recovery

topics.title: Inhalational Agents
topics.trap: Speed of induction follows the blood-gas coefficient, NOT the MAC — do not mix the two scales.

topics.oneLiner: Monitor the ulnar nerve, reverse non-depolarisers with neostigmine, rocuronium with sugammadex.
points: Suxamethonium is the only depolarising relaxant in routine use — fastest onset, shortest duration.
Non-depolarising agents include vecuronium, rocuronium, atracurium and pancuronium.
The ulnar nerve (adductor pollicis) is most commonly stimulated to monitor neuromuscular blockade.
Neostigmine reverses non-depolarising blockade; given with glycopyrrolate or atropine against muscarinic effects.
Sugammadex reverses rocuronium and vecuronium by encapsulating the molecule.
Atracurium releases histamine and degrades spontaneously (Hofmann elimination) — organ-independent.
Suxamethonium side effects: hyperkalaemia, bradycardia, raised intraocular pressure, malignant hyperthermia trigger.
Dale vasomotor reversal: adrenaline after alpha blockade causes a fall in BP from unopposed beta-2 vasodilation.
topics.title: Muscle Relaxants & Reversal
topics.trap: Neostigmine cannot reverse a depolarising (phase I) block — it can actually prolong it.

topics.askedAs: mechanism, Bier block drug, epidural anatomy
topics.oneLiner: Sodium channel blockade; Bier block takes lignocaine; the epidural needle stops before the dura.
points: Local anaesthetics block voltage-gated sodium channels from the intracellular side, stopping impulse conduction.
Small, unmyelinated C fibres (pain) are blocked before large myelinated motor fibres.
Intravenous regional anaesthesia (Bier block): lignocaine is the agent of choice.
Bupivacaine is never used for Bier block — accidental release causes severe cardiotoxicity.
Epidural needle traverses ligamentum flavum but does NOT puncture the dura mater.
Tuffier line joins the iliac crests and crosses the L4 spinous process — landmark for spinal/epidural.
Proparacaine is the topical local anaesthetic commonly used for cataract surgery.
Local anaesthetic toxicity: perioral numbness, tinnitus, convulsions, then cardiovascular collapse; treat with IV lipid emulsion.
Lignocaine with adrenaline is avoided in end-arterial areas: fingers, toes, penis, ear pinna.
topics.title: Local Anaesthetics & Regional Techniques
topics.trap: In an epidural the dura is the layer NOT pierced — piercing it is a spinal (or an accidental dural tap).

topics.oneLiner: 100-120 a minute, 5-6 cm deep; shock VF and pulseless VT, never asystole.
points: Adult chest compressions: rate 100-120 per minute, depth 5-6 cm, full recoil between compressions.
Single rescuer adult CPR ratio is 30 compressions to 2 breaths.
Shockable rhythms: ventricular fibrillation and pulseless ventricular tachycardia.
Asystole and pulseless electrical activity are non-shockable — continue CPR and give adrenaline.
Adrenaline in cardiac arrest: 1 mg IV every 3-5 minutes.
Defibrillation for VF/pulseless VT: biphasic shock 120-200 J, then immediate CPR for 2 minutes.
High-quality CPR minimises interruptions; switch compressors every 2 minutes to avoid fatigue.
BiPAP is contraindicated when the patient cannot protect the airway, e.g. reduced consciousness or facial trauma.
topics.title: BLS & ACLS Essentials
topics.trap: Asystole is not shocked — the answer is always CPR plus adrenaline, not defibrillation.

topics.oneLiner: Rigidity plus soaring temperature on halothane: stop the trigger, give dantrolene.
points: Malignant hyperthermia: halothane or suxamethonium triggers uncontrolled calcium release from sarcoplasmic reticulum.
Defective ryanodine receptor (RyR1) causes rigidity, hyperthermia, hypercarbia; treatment is dantrolene.
Capnography (end-tidal CO2) is the gold standard confirmation of tracheal intubation.
Earliest post-operative hypoxaemia with basal crepitations is most commonly atelectasis.
Accidental endobronchial intubation causes one-lung ventilation and collapse of the opposite lung.
Untreated hyperthyroid patient under anaesthesia risks thyroid storm — tachycardia, hyperthermia, arrhythmias.
Esmolol is the ultra-short-acting beta blocker, broken down by red-cell esterases.
Aspiration of gastric contents (Mendelson syndrome) is chemical pneumonitis — fasting rules exist to prevent it.
topics.title: Anaesthesia Emergencies & Monitoring
topics.trap: In malignant hyperthermia the earliest sign is rising end-tidal CO2, not fever — temperature rises late.
